name: John Hathorn
bio: A Representative from New York; born in Wilmington, Del., January 9, 1749; completed preparatory studies; surveyor by profession and a school teacher; served in the Revolutionary War, captain of the Colonial Militia; colonel of the Fourth Orange County (N.Y.) Regiment February 7, 1776, and served throughout the Revolutionary War; brigadier general of the Orange County Militia September 26, 1786; major general of New York state militia October 8, 1793; member of the New York assembly, 1778, 1780, 1782-1785, 1795, and 1805, and served as speaker in 1783 and 1784; served in the New York senate, 1786-1790 and 1799-1803; member of the council of appointment in 1787 and 1789; elected to the Confederation Congress in December 1788, but no further sessions were held; elected as an Anti-Administration candidate to the First Congress (March 4, 1789-March 3, 1791); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Second Congress in 1790; unsuccessful candidate for  election to the Third Congress in 1792; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Fourth Congress (March 4, 1795-March 3, 1797); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Fifth Congress in 1796; engaged in mercantile pursuits; died on February 19, 1825, in Warwick, Orange County, N.Y.; interment in the cemetery on the family estate; reinterment in Warwick Cemetery.
